Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front, then details and next steps below.

High level:
- Account-level no-training assurance: Redwood will not use customer request/response data to train or improve our models if the customer selects the "no-training" account setting or if contract explicitly includes the non-training attestation. This is the standard we offer for regulated customers on Hosted; Dedicated and Private default to customer-controlled training (i.e., Redwood does not train on data in Dedicated/Private unless explicitly contracted).
- Operational retention: default request/response payload retention for Hosted is 30 days; access and audit logs are retained 90 days by default. KV caches and inference caches are ephemeral and removed per instance lifecycle (seconds-minutes by default). Backups/snapshots are retained up to 90 days for incident recovery unless otherwise negotiated.
- Backups & snapshots: encrypted at rest, held in geographically-controlled regions per data residency settings. Backups are not used for training. Restoration is for recovery only and is governed by the same access controls.
- Deletion: deletion requests trigger a phased purge: live payloads are removed within 24–72 hours, caches evicted immediately, and backup/snapshot entries scheduled for removal at the next snapshot rotation (generally within 30–90 days depending on the retention policy). For contractual commitments we can shorten the backup retention window and provide signed attestation.

Attachments I'm including for your review: SOC2-summary.pdf (overview), deletion-playbook.pdf (internal steps and timelines), data-retention-matrix.xlsx (default and negotiable windows).

Next steps: 1) Ben and I can produce a one-page non-training attestation for signature, 2) if you want reduced backup windows we can surface a redline to the Dedicated/Hosted terms, 3) recommend a 30-minute call with your security + our security team to confirm PHI handling.

I'll let Ben add the security nitty-gritty.

Laura / Soojin — quick security clarifications and an operational note for PHI flows.

- Training: We do not and will not use customer payloads to train Redwood models for customers who opt into the no-training account setting or who have a contractual non-training clause. That applies to both raw payloads and derivative artifacts (we do not surface backups or snapshots to the model-training pipelines).
- Encryption & key management: all payloads and backups are encrypted with tenant-scoped keys. For Hosted customers we offer a customer-managed key (CMK) option via KMS; Dedicated/Private can integrate with on-prem HSMs.
- Access controls & auditability: restoration and access to backups are logged and audited. We can provide extended log retention (beyond default 90 days) for review as part of an evidence package, but those logs themselves are not used for training.
- Deletion playbook specifics: when a deletion request is submitted (API or legal), it's recorded and escalated to the data lifecycle pipeline: immediate live-data removal, KV/cache eviction, and a scheduled purge job for backups that removes snapshot blobs and updates manifests. For enterprise customers requesting faster backup purges we offer an SLA to guarantee removal within X days (we'll state a concrete number in the attestation).

Operational note: if your PHI processing requires absolute removal within 30 days from all copies (including backups), we can contractually commit to 30-day backup retention for your account and provide a signed attestation. That will require a limited change to our backup rotation policy for your tenant and a short onboarding checklist.

If helpful, I can include a sentence-by-sentence attestation ready for signature by legal.

— Ben Carter
